contracts.blurb: Neighbourhood frozen mall wants cartons of tilapia every week.
Twelve stores need labelled fish packs for their freezer aisle.
Hotel kitchens nationwide order cleaned catfish and stockfish.
Up-country distributors load reefer trucks with frozen cartons.
ECOWAS buyers want smoked catfish and crayfish by the pallet.
Diaspora shops abroad want certified, vacuum-packed smoked fish.

belt.name: Ice Conveyor Belt
belt.blurb: Chilled belt carries cleaned fish from the back to the counter.

auto.name: Pond Harvest Trawler
auto.blurb: Motorised net boat hauls tilapia and catfish from the ponds for you.

pack.name: Blast Freeze & Seal Line
pack.blurb: Blast freezes, vacuum seals and labels fish to export standard.

milestones.title: Second Depot Opens
milestones.blurb: Your first depot outside the market. One cold room, one freezer, big dreams.

milestones.title: Lagos Cold Room Network
milestones.blurb: Five depots across Lagos. Frozen-food malls now call you before they open.

milestones.title: Own Fish Hatchery
milestones.blurb: Ten depots need steady fish. You hatch your own fingerlings and stop begging farms.

milestones.title: Reefer Truck Fleet
milestones.blurb: Refrigerated trucks carry your cartons to the South-West without one fish thawing.

milestones.title: Modern Smoking Kilns
milestones.blurb: Clean smokeless kilns replace firewood drums. Your smoked catfish passes lab tests.

milestones.title: Nationwide Fish Brand
milestones.blurb: A depot in every state. Your label sits in freezers from Lagos to Maiduguri.

milestones.title: ECOWAS Seafood Hub
milestones.blurb: Depots in Ghana, Benin and Togo. Border paperwork knows your trucks by name.

milestones.title: Export Certified Plant
milestones.blurb: Your processing plant earns export approval. Containers leave Apapa port weekly.

milestones.title: Diaspora Freezer Favourite
milestones.blurb: African stores in London, Houston and Toronto stock your smoked fish packs.

milestones.title: Global Seafood Empire
milestones.blurb: 500 depots on three continents. From one basin of fish to a world seafood name.

staff: Abeg bring more ice, sun dey hot.
This catfish dey jump like dancer!
Cold room door, close am sharp sharp!
Customer, I go clean am for you.
Crayfish derica full to the brim!
Smoked fish just comot from kiln.
My hand don cold, but money dey warm.
Weigh am well, Madam dey watch.
Catfish wan escape from basin again!
Gen dey on, freezer dey happy.
customer: Give me two kilo of catfish.
Abeg cut am for pepper soup.
How much for one derica crayfish?
I need stockfish for my egusi.
Na here fish fresh pass for Lagos.
Add jara small now, Iya Sikira.
Pack am with ice, I dey go far.
Do you sell cartons? I get shop.
The catfish still dey move o!
I go send this one to my sister abroad.
manager: Madam, cold room dey at minus 18.
Reefer truck don reach the bay.
No break cold chain, I beg una.
Ice first, gist later, my people.
night: My hand still dey smell of fish.
Hope gen no off for cold room.
One basin then, cartons now. Wow.
Tomorrow I go buy another freezer.
This pepper soup na my own catfish.
One day, my fish go reach London.

events.name: Sunday Rice Rush
events.text: Everybody wants fried tilapia for Sunday rice. The queue reaches the road!

events.name: Generator Wahala
events.text: Cold room generator coughed all night. Diesel and repairs chop your money.

events.name: Bad Road to the Ponds
events.text: Rain spoil the farm road. Fish deliveries crawl in late today.

events.name: Owambe Weekend
events.text: Three big parties in town. Caterers pay top naira for catfish and stockfish.

events.name: Hot Sun, Slow Market
events.text: Sun too hot today. Customers stay indoors and the market is quiet.

events.name: Bumper Pond Harvest
events.text: The ponds overflow with fat fish. A bulk buyer clears the extra for cash.

events.name: Hotel Chef Visits
events.text: A big hotel chef comes shopping for seafood with a fat wallet.

events.name: New Ice Delivery
events.text: Ice block truck came early. Staff clean and pack fish double quick.

research.claim: Nigeria imports about 2.5 million tonnes of frozen fish a year, and local farms scale by adding their own hatchery, feed mill and drying ovens in place of roadside wood smoking.
Lagos processors began shipping branded smoked fish to the US after FDA lab tests of samples and an FDA Food Facility Registration number for the plant.
The US stopped smoked fish imports from Nigeria in March 2018 over documentation not supplied in time, so export paperwork and processing standards decide market access.
Industry reports say Nigeria needs at least 25,000 refrigerated trucks but has fewer than 1,000, with unreliable power a main cold-chain obstacle.
